header: A wrong "not stated" is a wrong answer. The model sometimes writes "Not stated in circular" in a comparison-table cell for an item that the circular DOES list (the 2025 holiday list names Bhatridwitiya on 23 October; the briefing said "Not stated"). I ask the model in the prompt not to do this, but this is the plain-code check that does not depend on the model obeying: for every "not stated" cell, I look up the item of that row in the text of the circular(s) of that column. If the circular names it, the cell is replaced by the circular's own words (a short quotation), never by a value the code makes up. Pure: no I/O, no model, the same input always gives the same output.

members.name: also
doc: Holds the sentence of the circular that also speaks of the item, when there is one beside the list entry ("... will be treated as additional Festival Holiday ...")

members.name: section
doc: Holds the kind of list that names the item ("restricted holiday"), when the circular's headings say so.

symbols.name: ConfirmedAbsence
doc: A "not stated" cell that I CHECKED against the circular of its column and found true: none of the item's names appears in that circular.

symbols.name: GENERIC
doc: These words name a kind of day or a category, not the item itself, so I never let them alone decide that "the circular names this item".

symbols.name: distinctiveWords
doc: I take the words of a row label that identify the item: at least 5 letters, and not a generic word.

symbols.name: sourcesOfColumn
symbols.sig: export function sourcesOfColumn(heading: string, sources: AbsenceSource[]): AbsenceSource[]
doc: Returns the sources a column of the table speaks of: those whose headline carries the column's heading ("2025"), or the year in it ("2025 Date" -> 2025). A heading that carries no year gives none.

symbols.name: entriesOf
symbols.sig: function entriesOf(flat: string): Array<{ from: number; to: number }>
doc: Gives the first and last character of every numbered table entry of a flattened text ("SL. No.: 28 | HOLIDAYS: ... | Day: Thursday").

symbols.name: clip
symbols.sig: const clip = (piece: string, max: number): string =>

symbols.name: readable
doc: A table entry as the text of the circular stores it ("HOLIDAYS: Rath Yatra | DATE: 27th June | Day: Friday") is read here as "Rath Yatra · 27th June · Friday": the values, in the circular's own words and order, without the column names.

symbols.name: sectionBefore
symbols.sig: function sectionBefore(flat: string, at: number): string | null
doc: I find the kind of list a table entry stands in from the nearest HEADING before it ("RESTRICTED HOLIDAYS (RH)", "FESTIVAL HOLIDAYS", "CLOSED/ PUBLIC HOLIDAYS"). It is said in the cell, so a reader does not take a restricted holiday for a festival holiday. Only a heading written in capitals counts (prose such as "treated as an additional Festival Holiday" is not a heading), and only when the entry numbers run on from the heading without starting over or jumping: a restart or a jump means another list began (or text is missing), and then I do NOT say the kind.

symbols.name: quoteFor
symbols.sig: function quoteFor(text: string, word: string, labelWords: string[] = []): { text: string; section: string | null; also?: string } | null
symbols.returns: { text: string; section: string | null; also?: string } | null
doc: Returns the circular's own words where the item is named: the table ENTRY that names it (one row; one with a figure preferred), AND the sentence that speaks of it outside any list, when there is one (the 2025 list names Bhatridwitiya as a restricted holiday, and a sentence says it "will be treated as additional Festival Holiday": the entry alone would mislead). With no entry, the sentence stands alone.

symbols.name: checkAbsences
symbols.sig: export function checkAbsences(table: SynthesisTable, sources: AbsenceSource[]): { table: SynthesisTable; fixes: AbsenceFix[]; confirmed: ConfirmedAbsence[] }
symbols.returns: { table: SynthesisTable; fixes: AbsenceFix[]; confirmed: ConfirmedAbsence[] }
doc: Replaces every "not stated" cell whose item the column's circular names by that circular's own words. I leave a cell alone when the column maps to no circular, when the row has no distinctive word, or when the circular does not contain it (a true "not stated").

symbols.name: sentencesOf
doc: Splits a text into sentences after a full stop followed by a capital letter, and at semicolons. Joined back with a space, nothing is lost.

symbols.name: mentions
symbols.sig: function mentions(sentence: string, fix: AbsenceFix): boolean

symbols.name: dropContradictedClaims
symbols.sig: export function dropContradictedClaims(text: string, fixes: AbsenceFix[]): { text: string; removed: string[] }
doc: Removes the sentences that say an item is absent for a column that the corrected table now shows as listed. `removed` has what was taken out.

symbols.name: shortHeadings
doc: Returns the column headings without the words they all share ("2024 Date", "2025 Date" -> "2024", "2025").

symbols.name: describeDifferences
symbols.sig: export function describeDifferences(table: SynthesisTable, fixes: AbsenceFix[], confirmed: ConfirmedAbsence[]): { text: string; sources: number[] } | null
